quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: Notice how the speaker's sentences break up.
quests.explanation: The good news is obvious, but the broken sentences and the need for a second show the shock is stronger than the pleasure. Surprise dominates.
quests.textToSpeak: Wait, you booked the whole restaurant? For me? I... okay, give me a second. I only came in for a coffee.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: Which feeling does the speaker say has 'sunk in'?
quests.explanation: The surprise was only the first reaction. What the speaker is left with, and acts on, is happiness.
quests.textToSpeak: I honestly didn't expect a promotion this year. But now that it's sunk in, I've got the biggest smile, and I've already called my mom twice.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: What is the speaker doing while the good news arrives?
quests.explanation: The speaker is still checking whether it's real, so disbelief outweighs pleasure. So surprised is the best fit.
quests.textToSpeak: The lottery site says I've won? Well, it's good news, obviously, but I'm still trying to work out whether I read the number right.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: Pay attention to what the speaker says after 'but'.
quests.explanation: The shaking hands are acknowledged, but the eagerness after 'but' is what defines the speaker's state. Excitement dominates.
quests.textToSpeak: Yes, my hands are shaking a little. But I've waited two years for this audition, and I wouldn't swap places with anyone in this building.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: What does the speaker have to talk themselves into?
quests.explanation: Needing to reassure themselves, and rereading with no plan, shows that unease about the call is the strongest feeling. That's what the clues add up to: nervousness.
quests.textToSpeak: I keep telling myself it's a great opportunity, and it is. But I've read the email six times, and I still don't know what I'll say when they call.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: Notice what the speaker has already done to get ready.
quests.explanation: The speaker accepts that it'll be hard but is already picturing themselves there. The speaker is excited.
quests.textToSpeak: Everyone says the first week at a new company is exhausting. I'm sure it will be. I've already picked out a plant for my desk.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: How does the speaker describe what they expected?
quests.explanation: There's some anger underneath, but the calm tone and 'I expected better' show a let-down more than hostility. Disappointment is the main feeling.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm not going to shout. They had months to fix it, and they knew how much it mattered to us. I just expected better from them.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: Notice the way the speaker judges the other person's behavior.
quests.explanation: The speaker doesn't just express regret. They accuse the reviewer of disrespect. That makes anger the strongest feeling.
quests.textToSpeak: Sure, I was hoping for a fair review. But you didn't even read my report, and then you criticized page four? That isn't a mistake. That's disrespect.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: What has the speaker run out of?
quests.explanation: The speaker is blocked by repeated failure and is out of ideas rather than aiming blame at someone. That's what the clues add up to: frustration.
quests.textToSpeak: Every time I explain the problem, they promise to fix it, and every time it comes back. I'm not angry. I've just run out of ways to say it differently.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: Which idea does the speaker repeat for emphasis?
quests.explanation: The exhaustion is real, but the repeated 'finally' shows the dominant feeling is the end of the pressure. Everything points to relief.
quests.textToSpeak: The last patient's gone, the report's filed, and the lights are off. I'm shattered, but at least it's finally, finally done.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: What does the speaker say they can't do at the moment?
quests.explanation: The good news is acknowledged, but the loss of basic memory shows that exhaustion is the dominant state.
quests.textToSpeak: The results are good, I know, and I'm glad. But I've been up for thirty hours, and right now I couldn't tell you my own address.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: Which sentence does the speaker repeat, and what does that show?
quests.explanation: The speaker's exhaustion is obvious, but the repeated reassurance about her health shows relief is the main feeling.
quests.textToSpeak: Three nights on a hospital sofa. She's asleep at last, breathing normally, and I can barely lift my head. She's fine. She's really fine.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: What is the speaker's problem with what happened?
quests.explanation: The speaker admits the achievement but focuses on the public attention. That's embarrassment.
quests.textToSpeak: My mother stood up in the middle of the restaurant and told everyone I'd won the prize. I mean, yes, I did. But could she have said it a little more quietly?

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: Catch what the speaker says they'd do again.
quests.explanation: The red ears show embarrassment, but standing tall and wanting a repeat show that pride is the main feeling.
quests.textToSpeak: It's silly, but when the mayor read my name out, my ears went red. Still, I walked up there straight-backed, and I'd do it again tomorrow.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: How does the speaker want to react?
quests.explanation: They appreciate the gesture but the wish to hide shows that embarrassment is stronger.
quests.textToSpeak: They put my drawing on the front of the newsletter with my name in big letters. Everyone at work has seen it. It's a lovely thing to do, but I'd like to hide until Friday.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: Which question comes after the thank-you?
quests.explanation: Surprise fits because the speaker's thanks is quick and the real reaction is disbelief.
quests.textToSpeak: You paid the whole bill? Wait. Nobody said anything. I mean, thank you, but... how did you even know I was here?

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: How does the speaker sum up the coworker's actions?
quests.explanation: The surprise is briefly mentioned, but the focus is on what was done and the wish to thank the person. Everything points to gratitude.
quests.textToSpeak: I didn't think anyone had noticed I was working late. But you did, and you brought dinner, and you stayed to help. I really don't know how to thank you.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: What does the speaker say about the agent's reason?
quests.explanation: After the initial doubt, the speaker recognizes the kindness behind the upgrade. That's what the clues add up to: gratitude.
quests.textToSpeak: When the agent said she'd upgrade us, I thought it was a mistake. It wasn't. She did it because we'd been traveling for two days. What a kind thing to do.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: Notice what the speaker says they are 'choosing' to do.
quests.explanation: The risk is real, but the speaker deliberately holds on to the good signs. That's what the clues add up to: hope.
quests.textToSpeak: Yes, the surgery is risky. But the doctor sounded sure, and the last scan was better than she'd expected. I'm choosing to believe this will work.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: Compare what the report says with what the speaker sees.
quests.explanation: The speaker wants to be hopeful but what they observe contradicts the good news. Worry is stronger.
quests.textToSpeak: They say the numbers are improving, and I want to believe that. But he's still not eating, and every time I visit, he's a little quieter.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: What small sign is the speaker holding on to?
quests.explanation: The speaker plays down expectations but points to one encouraging detail. This is hope.
quests.textToSpeak: The interview went okay, not brilliantly. I'm not counting on anything, but they did ask when I could start, so who knows?

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: Consider what the speaker refuses to do, despite the exhaustion.
quests.explanation: The speaker's body is worn out, but their attention is on the city and they won't rest. So excited is the best fit.
quests.textToSpeak: We've been traveling for nineteen hours, and I can barely feel my legs. But look at that skyline! I'm not sleeping for at least another three hours.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: Where does the speaker say they might watch from?
quests.explanation: Interest exists, but the plan to sit down shows that exhaustion is what actually decides what they'll do. That's tiredness.
quests.textToSpeak: Sure, the parade sounds amazing, and I'd love to see it. But I've had four hours' sleep, and honestly, I might watch it from the bench.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: Who does the speaker expect to arrive first, and why?
quests.explanation: The week is draining, but the speaker looks forward to the start with energy. Excitement is the feeling here.
quests.textToSpeak: It's been a long week, and tomorrow's even longer. But the new project kicks off at nine, and I'll be the first one there.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: Catch what the speaker says they want to do.
quests.explanation: The situation is puzzling, but the speaker moves toward finding out more. Everything points to curiosity.
quests.textToSpeak: This makes no sense. The lock is broken, the window's open, and nothing's missing. Somebody wanted to see something. I want to know what.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: Pay attention to what the speaker admits they can't do.
quests.explanation: Interest is there, but the inability to make sense of conflicting information is the dominant state.
quests.textToSpeak: Half of what he's saying is the opposite of what I heard in the meeting. I'm interested, don't get me wrong, but right now I couldn't explain any of it.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: What is the speaker looking for?
quests.explanation: The speaker is looking for an explanation, not overwhelmed by the puzzle. That's what the clues add up to: curiosity.
quests.textToSpeak: We've never seen the sky this color. Everyone's out in the street, and I've got my phone out. Someone must know what it is.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: Why does the speaker want to be quiet before telling anyone?
quests.explanation: Sitting quietly to let three weeks of pressure drain away shows relief rather than celebration.
quests.textToSpeak: The call's over, the contract's signed, and the last three weeks are finally behind me. I'm going to sit here quietly for a minute before I text anyone.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: Consider what the speaker wishes other people would do.
quests.explanation: Wanting other people to forget a public mishap is embarrassment.
quests.textToSpeak: I know I should laugh about it, and I will, eventually. But right now I'd like everyone who saw me fall off that stage to forget it happened.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: What does the speaker imagine, and how often?
quests.explanation: The speaker knows the chances are slim but keeps picturing the good outcome. This is hope.
quests.textToSpeak: I've sent the application. It's out of my hands now. It's a long shot, but I've read the acceptance email in my head about twenty times.
